name: Ben-Hadad
bio:
This Ben-Hadad, king of Syria, led thirty-two allied kings against Samaria in Ahab's reign — a later ruler than the earlier Ben-Hadad whom Asa had hired against Baasha a generation before. He first demanded Ahab's silver, gold, wives, and children, which Ahab conceded, then upped the demand to let his own servants ransack every house in Samaria for anything they pleased; Ahab, backed by the elders, refused this second demand. Enraged, Ben-Hadad boasted that Samaria's dust wouldn't fill the hands of his army, and Ahab answered, "Let not him that girdeth on his harness boast himself as he that putteth it off" (1 Kings 20:1-12).

A prophet told Ahab the LORD would hand him the vast army, and Israel's 232 young men routed Ben-Hadad's drunken forces, with Ben-Hadad himself escaping on a horse (1 Kings 20:13-21). The following year he returned with a reorganized army at Aphek, but Israel again crushed the Syrians — 100,000 footmen slain in a day and a further 27,000 killed when a wall collapsed on them at Aphek. Ben-Hadad's own servants, hearing Israel's kings were merciful, persuaded him to approach Ahab wrapped in sackcloth with ropes on their heads; Ahab called him "my brother," brought him up into his own chariot, and let him go after Ben-Hadad promised to restore captured cities and grant Israel trade access in Damascus (1 Kings 20:22-34). For releasing a man the LORD had appointed to complete destruction, Ahab was condemned by a disguised prophet, who told him his own life and people would answer for Ben-Hadad's (1 Kings 20:35-43).
